text:
maya: FYI console canary perf alert — interactive charts spike ~300-800ms when switching time range, seen after today's frontend bundle
sam: grabbing traces, linking when ready :eyes:
telemetry-bot: alert: chart-render-latency breached 250ms threshold on canary (10:12 UTC) — https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/8472
jordan: suspect culprit is the async-hooks polyfill merged this morning. build size +~120KB and a few hot functions look different in the profiler
liam: can you paste the bundle map or the `webpack --json` output? polyfills often trigger V8 deopts when they replace native shapes
maya: repro steps: 1) open /metrics 2) select 30d -> 1h view 3) toggle compare. attaching perf snapshot from my dev session (screencap + CPU profile)
sam: trace shows repeated long tasks on main thread ~180-240ms and GC pauses aligned with those tasks. stack top points to ChartRenderer.render -> formatTimeBuckets -> runtime-helpers from the new polyfill
anya: noticed KV prefix cache miss rate jumped at the same time. a lot more backend fetches which cause component state churn + re-render storms
jordan: one more thing — routing policy fallback for quota pressure routes users to legacy-renderer path. if the client hits 429 the retry logic re-invokes the heavy render path, doubling work
sam: here's the client snippet from `chartClient.ts` showing the retry behavior:
```
async function fetchData() {
  const res = await fetch(url);
  if (res.status === 429) {
    await sleep(1000);
    return fetchData();
  }
  return res.json();
}
```
liam: yeah that recursion + fallback renderer = worst-case cascade. also the polyfill adds hidden classes that make `formatTimeBuckets` much slower in our hot loop
maya: proposed action items:
- revert async-hooks polyfill on canary and run perf baseline
- change chart-data client to avoid immediate retry on 429 for time-series routes (treat as soft-failure and surface degraded UI)
- add telemetry markers around fetch/retry/render boundaries for better tracing
- investigate KV prefix cache hot keys and add targeted prefetching
sam: I'll open two PRs: 1) revert polyfill canary revert PR, 2) client retry change (non-retriable for /v1/chart-data). will also add a perf job to CI to capture the 30d->1h toggle case
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: revert PR #3141 -> canary at 2026-03-20T13:00:00Z (by @sam)
jordan: also worth tuning quota token-bucket burst window — current config causes short 429 storms during dashboard load bursts
anya: I'll dig into KV cache telemetry and list top N keys by miss rate, will try a small prefetch for top 5 queries
maya: thanks team. I'll post before/after screenshots and perf numbers in #perf-dashboard and assign follow-ups in the tracker
sam: will also add a small synthetic test that toggles the range repeatedly to catch regressions in PR checks
liam: :eyes: keep me posted if you need a quick revert on prod
maya: cheers :thumbsup:
